clue.text: Saddam extremely ready to organise volunteer force

indicators.note: organising puts a jumble into a new order, so the gathered letters are rearranged
extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the two end letters of ready

explanation.surface: Saddam Hussein, primed for action, musters an irregular army of volunteers.
explanation.walkthrough: DAD'S ARMY is the British sitcom about the Home Guard, the Second World War's volunteer defence force of older men.
explanation.definitionFit: The Home Guard was a part-time unpaid militia, affectionately nicknamed after the television comedy about one platoon.

clue.text: Little girl provided water and light

definitions.note: light in its old sense of alight, get down

parts.note: Di is a short form of Diana
sent as in supplied or dispatched
rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: A small girl supplied water and a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: Light is a verb here, the old sense of alight, to get down from a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To disentrain is to get off a train, to alight from it, and light once meant alight.

clue.text: They may provide extensive work for the plumber

definitions.text: They may provide extensive work for the plumber

parts.words: They may provide extensive work for the plumber
parts.note: surface reading: big jobs for a tradesman who fixes pipes

parts.words: They may provide extensive work for the plumber
parts.note: setter's reading: a plumber is one who plumbs, sounding depth with a weighted line, and profound seas need a long line

explanation.walkthrough: To plumb is to measure depth with a lead weight on a line, so a plumber here is a depth-sounder.
explanation.definitionFit: Profound stretches of sea are where a sounding line must go furthest; figuratively the phrase also means serious trouble.

clue.text: Laser surgery in France

definitions.note: a place in France rather than the phrase itself

indicators.note: surgery cuts things up and rearranges them, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Laser eye operations performed at a French clinic.
explanation.definitionFit: Arles is a Provence town on the Rhône, famous for its Roman arena and Van Gogh.

clue.text: Change socks after mad team romp

indicators.note: mad means crazed or disordered, so the letters go out of their order

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings or socks

explanation.surface: Players swap their socks after a wild team frolic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the socks second, after the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To metamorphose is to transform completely, as a caterpillar does into a butterfly.

clue.text: Inventor is back for the finish at Twickenham

indicators.note: something back to front is read from its end, so the rugby phrase runs right to left

parts.note: no side is the referee's call ending a rugby match; Twickenham is England's rugby stadium

explanation.surface: An inventor returns to watch the end of a rugby international.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is back' reads as the inventor returning, but it tells you to turn NO SIDE around to get EDISON.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison patented the phonograph and a practical electric light bulb, making him the archetypal American inventor.

clue.text: A great many turn up to assist a farm hand

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a myriad is a vast number

explanation.surface: Crowds arrive to help someone working on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairymaid is a woman employed on a farm to milk cows and make butter.

clue.text: Son in whom Adam set his hope?

parts.note: surface padding that sets the biblical scene

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: found running across these two words

explanation.surface: A biblical question about which child Adam pinned his hopes on.
explanation.walkthrough: After Cain killed Abel, Seth was the son through whom Adam's line continued, so the surface also points at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Seth was the third son of Adam and Eve in Genesis.

clue.text: Fireside bower

parts.note: surface reading: a leafy shelter or nook next to the hearth
setter's reading: one who drew a bow across strings beside a blaze, the emperor said to have fiddled while Rome burned

explanation.walkthrough: Read bower as one who bows a fiddle; the legend says this Roman emperor fiddled while his city burned in AD 64.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor of legend played music beside the great fire of Rome, so he is the player by the flames.

clue.text: Let's reflect after dark, like the stars

indicators.note: a mirror reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: late at night is after dark

explanation.surface: An invitation to sit and think after nightfall, gazing up at the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellate means star-shaped, radiating points from a centre as stars appear to.

clue.text: Not indulging in German beer, get British ale

indicators.note: in places the abstaining word inside the German word for beer

parts.note: TT is teetotal, abstaining from drink

explanation.surface: A drinker turns down lager in Germany but happily orders a British pint.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter is the classic hoppy draught beer served in British pubs, a style of pale ale.

clue.text: Parisienne, she goes to city in Great Britain — wearing a bikini?

definitions.note: describes the answer rather than naming it

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England

explanation.surface: A French woman travels to a British resort, perhaps in a swimsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisienne, she' means she in a Parisian's French. 'Goes to' puts her after the city part.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathing belle is an attractive woman in swimwear at the seaside, so someone in a bikini fits.

clue.text: Points total girl achieved with basic intelligence

parts.note: the four compass points, north, east, west, south

explanation.surface: A girl tots up her score in a quiz needing only general knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: Intelligence here means information, as in military intelligence, not brainpower.
explanation.definitionFit: A news summary gives the bare essentials of current information, the headlines without the detail.

clue.text: Rise of an establishment holding exotic dances

indicators.note: holding means gripping something inside, so the short word wraps the jumble
exotic means strange and foreign, so the letters appear in an unfamiliar order

parts.note: the Establishment can mean the Church of England, CE

explanation.surface: A venue becomes popular because it stages foreign dances.
explanation.walkthrough: The Church of England is the established church, so the Establishment can stand for CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascendance is a rising up or gaining of dominance, a noun close in sense to rise.

clue.text: Foreshadows one being speechless over old council tax

parts.note: rates were the British local property tax replaced by the community charge and then council tax

explanation.surface: A ratepayer, struck dumb by the old local tax, hints at worse to come.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first parts above the tax. Council tax is the British local levy on homes.
explanation.definitionFit: To adumbrate is to give a faint outline or indication in advance, which is what foreshadowing does.

clue.text: Tries alternative services

indicators.note: an alternative version is a different arrangement, so the letters are shuffled into another order

explanation.surface: Someone sampling different forms of worship, or a rugby team scoring other ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Rites are religious ceremonies, the formal observances held in church services.

clue.text: Ford gains in performance — real cool

indicators.note: a performance puts things through their paces in a new show, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Ford car's speed improves on the road test, impressively calm and smooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Sang-froid, French for cold blood, is composure under pressure, genuine coolness of nerve.

clue.text: Last vehicle held by danger signal went through

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it, so the vehicle sits within the signal

parts.note: red is the colour of a stop or danger light
the last vehicle anyone rides in is the hearse at their funeral

explanation.surface: A final car stopped by a red warning light before it passed through.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse a play is to run through it in practice, so went through is past tense rehearsed.

clue.text: Kent opener ran him out — an eminent player

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so the letters are rearranged
an opener comes first, so only the initial letter of the county is taken

explanation.surface: A cricket report: Kent's opening batsman was run out by a star bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface 'out' is a cricket dismissal; Kent is an English county side. 'an' belongs to the letters as well as the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Imran Khan captained Pakistan to the 1992 cricket World Cup and is among the finest all-rounders the sport has seen.

clue.text: Vision of dam-busting engineer

indicators.note: busting into something breaks inside it, so the engineer sits within the barrier

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps

explanation.surface: Recalls Barnes Wallis, the engineer whose bouncing bomb burst German dams.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is a vision seen in sleep, or an imagined hope for the future.

clue.text: Rabbit's pile?

parts.note: surface reading: a heap belonging to a rabbit, perhaps its droppings or burrow
setter's reading: a pile is a nuclear reactor, and rabbits reproduce quickly, so this is a reactor type named for prolific reproduction

explanation.walkthrough: Pile is an old word for a nuclear reactor; a rabbit breeds fast, so its pile would be the reactor named after quick breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: This reactor generates more fissile material than it consumes, breeding fuel using fast neutrons, the opposite of slow moderated designs.

clue.text: Fear getting topped by mistake

indicators.note: topping something cuts off its head, and in a down clue the top is the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone frightened of being executed through some blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, something done wrongly by accident.

clue.text: Upset plans to provide wartime diet

indicators.note: upset means turned over, and in a down clue that reads the word bottom to top

parts.note: maps are plans of an area

explanation.surface: Disrupted arrangements for feeding people during a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam, the tinned pork, was a staple of rationed Second World War meals in Britain.

clue.text: It's said to be wrong, dropping one at the millennium

indicators.note: dropping something leaves it behind, so those letters are removed from the word

explanation.surface: A claim that something is wicked, dropping a single item around the year 2000.
explanation.walkthrough: IMMORAL loses I followed by MM, the year 2000 that marked the millennium.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken rather than written, so an oral statement is one that is said.

clue.text: Vicar responsible for a little petty crime

indicators.note: a little of the word means just a small piece of it, its opening letter

parts.note: arson is the crime of setting fires deliberately

explanation.surface: A clergyman turns out to be behind some minor wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Petty crime' reads as one phrase, but petty only gives its first letter, and the crime is hardly petty.
explanation.definitionFit: A parson is a parish priest in the Church of England, the same office a vicar holds.

clue.text: Music maker, one in central presentation

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the reworked word
a presentation sets things out in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A musician performs solo at the heart of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is a woodwind instrument, something a player uses to make music.

clue.text: Sickness of a young man in springtime

indicators.note: in places the youth inside the name of the spring month

parts.note: a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: Lovesickness striking a youth in spring, when his fancy turns to love.
explanation.definitionFit: A malady is an illness or ailment, a formal word for being unwell.

clue.text: Courageous nobleman in band

indicators.note: in places the titled man inside the heraldic stripe

parts.note: a fess is a broad horizontal band across a heraldic shield

explanation.surface: A brave aristocrat plays in a pop group.
explanation.walkthrough: Band looks like a group of musicians, but here it is the heraldic stripe.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearless means showing no fear, which is what it is to be brave or courageous.
